goal: Independently verify that Massar's four hard safety invariants hold in the committed engine: the customer opt-out path cannot be swallowed, the Gupshup webhook authenticates, no secret literal is committed, and no outbound WhatsApp send can bypass the send guard. These are CLAUDE.md §3's safety booleans — all must hold.

scope.note: Server-side only. The dashboard template literal (src/dashboard.ts) is out of scope for this manifest — it carries no send path and no auth.

acceptance_criteria.text: A bare customer opt-out ('إيقاف', 'ايقاف', 'STOP', 'unsubscribe', …) short-circuits every other turn handling: it is matched before any model call, it cannot be consumed by an earlier branch, and it terminates further outbound messaging for that contact. Anchor: OPT_OUT_BARE at src/agent.ts:756 and its handler at :859.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Quote the matching branch and show, by reading the control flow above it, that no earlier return or condition can swallow an opt-out message.

acceptance_criteria.text: The Gupshup webhook rejects unauthenticated requests. Assess src/index.ts:32 — 'if (cfg.webhookToken && token !== cfg.webhookToken)' — specifically for its behaviour when WEBHOOK_TOKEN is unset or empty, and state plainly whether the route then accepts unauthenticated POSTs.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Quote the guard and the config default it reads (src/config.ts:20), then state the outcome for an empty token.

acceptance_criteria.text: No API key, token, or credential literal appears in the committed tree. Values must come from process.env only.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Name every file that reads a secret and confirm each reads it from process.env rather than a literal.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every outbound WhatsApp path runs through the single guarded send function; no call site reaches the Gupshup wire directly, bypassing opt-out, window, and turn-cap checks.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Enumerate all call sites that reach the Gupshup send wire and show each passes the guard.
